suggested.name: Darbaranyeswarar (Saneeswaran) Temple, Thirunallar
suggested.what: The most important Saturn temple. King Nala was freed from Saturn's affliction here; devotees apply sesame oil and bathe in Nala Theertham before darshan. Very crowded on Saturdays and at Shani Peyarchi (Saturn's sign change; the latest was 6 March 2026, Aquarius → Pisces).

suggested.name: Shani Shingnapur
suggested.deity: Shani as a self-manifested black stone, open to the sky
suggested.what: Devotees do tail-abhishek (oil poured over the stone) to ease Sade Sati and Dhaiya. Shani Amavasya (new moon on a Saturday) is the biggest day. Since 2025 the trust accepts only branded oil.

suggested.name: Apatsahayesvarar Temple, Alangudi
suggested.what: Jupiter (Guru) shrine. Thursdays are crowded; huge gatherings at Guru Peyarchi (Jupiter's sign change). Tradition asks devotees to stay at least one lagna (about 2½ hours).

suggested.name: Naganathaswamy Temple, Thirunageswaram
suggested.deity: Shiva as Naganatha; Rahu with his two consorts
suggested.what: Rahu shrine. Milk abhishekam to Rahu during Rahu Kalam – the milk is seen turning bluish as it flows over the idol. Sundays are special. Offerings: urad dal and blue cloth. Sought for Kaal Sarp / sarpa dosha, marriage obstacles and childlessness.

suggested.name: Trimbakeshwar Jyotirlinga
suggested.what: The best-known place for Kaal Sarp shanti and for Narayan Nagbali (a 3-day rite for pitra dosha) and Tripindi shraddha. These are done by Trimbak's priests in the town; only Rudrabhishek is done inside the temple.
suggested.when: dates fixed by nakshatra – book with a priest

suggested.name: Srikalahasti Temple
suggested.what: Famous Rahu–Ketu Sarpa Dosha Nivarana Puja, held daily; doing it in Rahu Kalam is preferred. Also sought for marriage delay and progeny.

suggested.name: Kukke Subramanya Temple
suggested.what: India's foremost temple for sarpa / naga dosha. Sarpa Samskara is a 2-day rite (₹4,200 on the temple's site); Ashlesha Bali is done on Ashlesha nakshatra days. Also sought by childless couples.

suggested.name: Siddhavat & Ram Ghat
suggested.what: Pitra dosh pind daan and tarpan, and Kaal Sarp shanti, on the Kshipra banks (not inside Mahakaleshwar's sanctum). Combines well with Mangalnath.

suggested.name: Garbharakshambigai Temple, Thirukarukavur
suggested.deity: Parvati as protector of the womb
suggested.what: Visited by couples praying for a child and for safe pregnancy: ghee blessed at the goddess's feet is taken for 48 days; castor oil is given for a safe delivery.

suggested.name: Naganathaswamy Temple, Keezhaperumpallam
suggested.what: Ketu shrine of the Navagraha circuit.

directory.name: Suryanar Kovil
directory.what: The Sun temple of the Navagraha circuit; the only one where Surya is the main deity, with shrines for all nine grahas. Good first stop of the circuit.

directory.name: Kailasanathar Temple, Thingalur
directory.what: Moon (Chandra) shrine of the Navagraha circuit, for an afflicted or weak Moon and peace of mind.

directory.name: Vaitheeswaran Koil
directory.what: Mars (Angaraka) shrine. Shiva here is the 'God of healing'; a dip in the Siddhamirtham tank is believed to cure disease. Also known for Nadi palm-leaf astrology.

directory.name: Swetharanyeswarar Temple, Thiruvenkadu
directory.what: Mercury (Budha) shrine of the Navagraha circuit – for learning, speech and trade.

directory.what: Venus (Shukra) shrine – for marriage, comforts and relationships.

directory.name: Navagraha Mandir, Chitrachal Hill
directory.what: Built in 1752 by Ahom king Rajeshwar Singha. Nine Shiva-lingas, one per graha, each draped in its colour, with the Sun at the centre – worship of all nine together.

directory.name: Mangalnath Temple
directory.what: Held to be the birthplace of Mars (Matsya Purana). Known for Bhat Puja (offering of cooked rice) for Manglik / Kuja dosha, usually before marriage; also Angarak dosha shanti.

directory.name: Shree Mangal Graha Mandir
directory.what: One of the rare temples dedicated to Mars itself; red lentils are the main offering.

directory.name: Somnath Jyotirlinga
directory.deity: Shiva as Somnatha, 'Lord of the Moon'
directory.what: Tradition holds that the Moon was freed from Daksha's curse here by worshipping Shiva (with the Mahamrityunjaya mantra) – the classic tirtha for a weak or afflicted Moon.

directory.name: Vishnupad Temple & Phalgu river, Gaya
directory.what: The foremost place for pind daan and shraddha; Pitru Paksha mela every Ashwin. Rites begin on the Phalgu and continue at Vishnupad and the other vedis.

directory.name: Brahma Kapal, Badrinath
directory.what: Pind daan on the ghat behind the Badrinath temple; open only in the Char Dham season.

directory.name: Prithudak Tirtha, Pehowa
directory.what: A major place for pind daan for ancestors on the Saraswati; family genealogy registers are kept here. Closest of these to Himachal.

directory.name: Siddhavat & Ram Ghat
directory.what: Pitra dosh pind daan and tarpan, and Kaal Sarp shanti, on the Kshipra banks (not inside Mahakaleshwar's sanctum). Combines well with Mangalnath.

directory.name: Kalyana Sundareswarar Temple, Thirumanancheri
directory.deity: Shiva and Parvati in their wedding form
directory.what: Where Shiva married Parvati – the 'marriage temple' for delayed marriage. Devotees offer garlands; the garland received back is kept at home and returned to the temple by the couple after the wedding.

directory.name: Garbharakshambigai Temple, Thirukarukavur
directory.deity: Parvati as protector of the womb
directory.what: Visited by couples praying for a child and for safe pregnancy: ghee blessed at the goddess's feet is taken for 48 days; castor oil is given for a safe delivery.

directory.name: Maa Baglamukhi Temple, Bankhandi
directory.place: near Dehra, Kangra (~35–40 km from Kangra)
directory.what: A siddha-peetha of Bagalamukhi, the Mahavidya linked to Mars in tantra-jyotish. Havans here are sought for protection, disputes and court cases. Near Jwalamukhi and Chintpurni – the closest of these temples to Mandi.

principles.text: Identification (tadatmya): a mantra works when the practitioner becomes one with its devata – recite with that feeling, not mechanically.
Unbroken practice (abhyasa-nairantarya): once begun, keep the daily count without a break; a broken practice loses its momentum.
Sankalpa and single-minded devotion: take a clear resolve before starting and hold to one deity and one mantra.
Give up glani (despondency): dejection drains all capacity; it is overcome by fresh inner awakening (unmesha), not by force.
Inner worship is the highest: tantra's ideal is manasi (mental) and symbolic puja – outer ritual is a support, not the goal.
Offer the ten flowers: compassion, forgiveness, sense-restraint, knowledge, good deeds, non-harming, conduct, the Self, joy and honouring fellow seekers – these are the real offerings.
Diksha from a guru is central to mantra sadhana in the book; so this app lists only a Mahavidya's names, stotras and inner worship – take her mantra from a guru.

ten_flowers.verse: दयापुष्पं क्षमापुष्पं पुष्पमिन्द्रियनिग्रहम्। ज्ञानपुष्पं पुण्यपुष्पमहिंसापुष्पमुत्तमम्॥ आचारपुष्पं मे देवि स्वयंभूपुष्पमुत्तमम्। आनन्दपुष्पं दातव्यं पुष्पञ्च साधकार्चनम्॥
ten_flowers.source: Tara Rahasya, quoted in the book p. 391
